question.text: An organic compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math>' <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi><mn>9</mn></msub><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">H</mi><mn>10</mn></msub><mi mathvariant="normal">O</mi></mrow></mfenced></math> when treated with conc. <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>HI</mi></math> undergoes cleavage to yield compound '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>' and '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>'. '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">B</mi></math>' gives yellow precipitate with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mtext>AgNO</mtext><mn>3</mn></msub></math> where as '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math>' tautomerizes to '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math>'. '<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">D</mi></math>' gives positive iodoform test. solution.text: Benzene ring should not be attached to O atom otherwise it will yield phenol after reacting withHI so third option is prefect which gives benzyl iodide and it gives yellow precipitate of AgI after reacting with AgNO3. Another product tautomerises and gives acetaldehyde which gives iodoform test.
